question: What is the key architectural difference between RAG and MCP tools for data access?
options: RAG retrieves unstructured knowledge from documents while MCP tools access structured data and perform operations through external APIs
RAG works only with voice agents while MCP tools work with any LLM application
RAG requires a vector database while MCP tools require a relational database
RAG is faster while MCP tools are more accurate
explanation: RAG retrieves unstructured knowledge (documents, policies, manuals) from a vector database. MCP tools access structured data (customer records, calendar events, database rows) and can perform write operations (schedule appointments, update records). Combining both gives an agent comprehensive access to knowledge and actions.

question: Why are clear, specific tool descriptions critical for MCP tool integration?
options: Vague descriptions cause the MCP server to reject tool registration
The LLM decides whether and when to call a tool based entirely on the tool's name and description
Tool descriptions are displayed to the end user before the tool is executed
The MCP protocol requires descriptions to be at least 50 characters long
explanation: The LLM has no other way to understand what a tool does besides its name and description. A vague description like 'look up data' will cause incorrect tool calls. A precise description like 'Look up a customer by email address. Returns name, plan, and account status.' helps the model make the right decision about when and how to use the tool.
